tools.name: access_check
tools.description:
Probe Local → ACCESS SSH connectivity with short timeouts (≤10s). Structured JSON: reachable, latencyMs, host, port, auth.

AccessTransport only (MCP client → SSH → ACCESS). Does NOT run kubectl or touch hop-2 hosts. Uses an ephemeral SSH session.

When to use: first session; VPN/network unsure; after ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE.
When NOT to use: cluster/kubectl health (shell_exec cluster-info); pod ops.
If reachable=false (code ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE): stop THIS YAML link (VPN / ACCESS_HOST). Other descriptions may still work. Negative TTL may return a cached failure without re-probing.
Example: {} or {"description":"<exact link>"}

Example: {"command":"hostname"} or {"host":"10.0.0.5","command":"hostname"}

tools.name: remote_copy_file
tools.description:
Synchronous copy. Endpoints: target=local (MCP machine), target=remote (selected Linux), target=pod (kubectl on that Linux).

Select the Linux with description + optional host (same as shell_exec). Paradi: no hop-2.
Large/long copies: remote_copy_start, not this tool.
Example: {"source":{"target":"remote","path":"/etc/hostname"},"dest":{"target":"local","path":"C:/tmp/hostname"}}

target.description: local = MCP machine; remote = selected Linux (description + optional host); pod = kubectl on that Linux

recursive.description: Directory copy (default true). local↔remote walks files; Runtime uses cp -a / scp -r / kubectl cp.

skipIfComplete.description: Skip rewrite when destination already matches. Gate strength = verify: size (cheap) or size+sha256 (content). Incompatible with verify=none.

totalTimeoutMs.description: Hard wall-clock limit for the whole copy (falls back to timeoutMs / DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS)

verify.description: Verification / skip gate (default size). size=cheap size match; size+sha256=content (files + directories per-file). none forbidden with skipIfComplete.

tools.name: remote_copy_cancel
tools.description:
Cancel a running/queued async copy job by transferId.

Aborts the in-process worker: local↔remote SFTP sessions end promptly; kubectl cp / scp on landing is best-effort.
Already-finished jobs are left unchanged (terminal status is fenced).
Example: {"transferId":"copy-xxx"}

instructions:
You are connected to host-execution-mcp.

Execution model:
  Access: MCP client → SSH → this YAML link's landing (ACCESS_HOST)
  Runtime: shell / docker / kubectl / copy on that landing
  Second hop: pass host (IP reachable FROM ACCESS). Omit host = stay on the landing.
  This tool path is ACCESS→host, not laptop SSH.

Tools:
- access_check — Local→ACCESS probe (≤10s; NOT kubectl). First session / after ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE
- shell_exec — command on the selected machine (omit host = landing; pass host = hop-2)
- context_probe / docker_* / k8s_* / remote_* — same pick: description + optional host
- remote_read_file / remote_ps — path on that machine; add namespace+pod to go into a container via kubectl there
- remote_copy_* — endpoints target=local|remote|pod; remote/pod use the same selected machine

Hard rules:
- access_check.reachable=false or code=ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE → stop THIS link (VPN / ACCESS_HOST). Other YAML descriptions may still work.
- SSH success ≠ docker/kubectl; unknown ≠ true — never invent true; never reuse capabilities across machines
- Before pkill/kill/rm: remote_ps or user confirmation
- Never assume namespace/paths; never reuse ACCESS_USER as hop-2 user
- success=false: read stdout (stderr merged). truncated → more lines / remote_copy_*
- Multi-container pods: pass container name
- Once per conversation: listResources and read host-execution://guides/user, host-execution://guides/agent, and host-execution://guides/yaml. GUIDE is the capability the user wants; if a tool cannot meet it, tell the user. Reuse for the session — do not look for repo file paths.
YAML roster: ~/.agents/host-execution.yaml (Windows %USERPROFILE%\.agents\host-execution.yaml). Same link = user+IP. New user+IP in conversation → append unless the user says not to. Same conversation keeps the current link. Roster is empty — tell the user to append a link from host-execution://guides/yaml. description is a scenario label, not a frozen key — if it is misleading, rewrite it in the YAML now and then pass the new exact string. Do not invent fields — copy from host-execution://guides/yaml.
